Iluvatar launched TianGai 300 at WAIC on July 19, 2026, as the first product of a new in-house architecture. The timing fits the prospectus's TG Gen 4 plan (launch Q2 2026, mass production Q3 2026), not TG Gen 3 (launched Q3 2024). Mass production is unconfirmed; fabrication remains undisclosed.

The issuer prospectus records ZK Gen1 launch in December 2022 and mass production in February 2023; the current product page identifies ZK100. SOPHGO's company timeline describes BM1690 as a 2024 large-model training/inference processor, and its software release history documents BM1690 support. Foundry, node, and physical campus are undisclosed.

products.notes: Tesla's in-house AI chip. Musk said in October 2025 that it was for cars and robots, with surplus chips for Tesla's data centers, and in April 2026, when it taped out, that its initial focus is Optimus and Tesla's supercomputer clusters. He said in July 2025 that TSMC would make AI5 first in Taiwan and then in Arizona, and in October 2025 that Samsung in Texas and TSMC in Arizona would both make it. In July 2026 a Samsung Foundry engineer wrote, in a post later deleted, that the Samsung version had taped out and would be made at Taylor on Samsung's 2 nm process; the TSMC version taped out earlier, and its node is not disclosed. Musk has pointed to mass production by mid-2027; the reviewed sources report no volume production as of August 25, 2026.

Tesla's successor to AI5. Musk said in January 2026 that AI6 is for Optimus and data centers. He said in July 2025 that Samsung's new Texas fab would be dedicated to AI6, in November 2025 that AI6 would use the same fabs as AI5, and in April 2026 that AI6 would use Samsung's 2 nm fab in Texas while AI6.5 would use TSMC 2 nm in Arizona (AI6.5 is not listed; see AIREV-0401). Samsung disclosed a matching $16.5 billion contract through 2033 without naming the customer. Reported production timing ranges from late 2027 to 2028; no data-center share is given.

product.notes: Tesla's in-house AI chip. Musk said in October 2025 that it was for cars and robots, with surplus chips for Tesla's data centers, and in April 2026, when it taped out, that its initial focus is Optimus and Tesla's supercomputer clusters. He said in July 2025 that TSMC would make AI5 first in Taiwan and then in Arizona, and in October 2025 that Samsung in Texas and TSMC in Arizona would both make it. In July 2026 a Samsung Foundry engineer wrote, in a post later deleted, that the Samsung version had taped out and would be made at Taylor on Samsung's 2 nm process; the TSMC version taped out earlier, and its node is not disclosed. Musk has pointed to mass production by mid-2027; the reviewed sources report no volume production as of August 25, 2026.

product.notes: Tesla's in-house AI chip. Musk said in October 2025 that it was for cars and robots, with surplus chips for Tesla's data centers, and in April 2026, when it taped out, that its initial focus is Optimus and Tesla's supercomputer clusters. He said in July 2025 that TSMC would make AI5 first in Taiwan and then in Arizona, and in October 2025 that Samsung in Texas and TSMC in Arizona would both make it. In July 2026 a Samsung Foundry engineer wrote, in a post later deleted, that the Samsung version had taped out and would be made at Taylor on Samsung's 2 nm process; the TSMC version taped out earlier, and its node is not disclosed. Musk has pointed to mass production by mid-2027; the reviewed sources report no volume production as of August 25, 2026.

sites.notes: The Arizona campus is operating with several expansion phases. Do not infer that every N4, N3, N2, or A16 product is assigned here; each exact-campus product claim requires its own source. Node candidates here are an editorial selection: products on TSMC N4P and NVIDIA's custom 4N/4NP processes. TSMC's Arizona page documents N4 volume production, and NVIDIA's 4NP Blackwell is made here. TSMC's 2025 Form 20-F lists 5 nm as Fab 21's most advanced volume-production technology, but no reviewed source shows N5 itself running here, so products disclosed only as TSMC N5 are not listed; this is not evidence that Arizona cannot run N5.

all_product_relationships.caveat: April 2025 expert testimony reports SMIC producing Ascend 910B dies at about 20 percent yield and calls SN2 China's only active 7 nm line; the campus link combines these statements and is not a first-party allocation. The same testimony reports, citing government officials, that TSMC made more than 2 million 910B dies, and the sources reviewed do not confirm production after April 2025.

exact_campus_allocation.notes: Written statement by Gregory C. Allen (CSIS) for the April 8, 2025, House Science, Space, and Technology Committee hearing 'DeepSeek: A Deep Dive'; it states that the views are Allen's own, not those of CSIS or the Committee. It says SMIC's SN2 facility is 'the sole facility in China with an active 7 nm logic chip production line', that SN1 focuses on 14 nm, and that SMIC calls its 7 nm node 'N+2'. It reports 'SMIC's 20 percent yield when producing Ascend 910Bs' and says TSMC made more than 2 million 910B dies. The Ascend-to-SN2 link combines these statements; the testimony does not name the module that made specific dies. Supports review decision add_P2 for Ascend 910B at SN2.
exact_campus_allocation.publisher: Gregory C. Allen, testimony to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology
exact_campus_allocation.title: DeepSeek: A Deep Dive

product.notes: Split from Ascend 910C. CSET's independent analysis supports an SMIC 7 nm-class/N+2 attribution for 910B and documents use in 2024. Reuters (October 2024) reports that TechInsights found a TSMC-made die in a 910B, so no single foundry is asserted. April 2025 expert testimony reports SMIC producing 910B dies and calls SN2 China's only active 7 nm line; the Atlas combines these into a P2 (not first-party) SN2 link, and current 2026 availability was not revalidated.

sites.inclusion_rationale: A Pudong planning record filed by SMIC Shanghai places the SN1/SN2 plant project on SMIC's four-road Zhangjiang block, where SMIC also lists its Shanghai 200 mm and 300 mm fabs. Reviewed evidence supports 14 nm capability at SN1 and reported 7 nm-class (N+2) capability at SN2; expert testimony links SMIC-made Ascend 910B dies to SN2.

coordinate_source.notes: Nominatim returns 31.2172620, 121.6024705 as the representative point for the SMIC-named industrial feature. The point is a location-only search anchor, not a computed centroid, surveyed boundary, module-capability source, or product-allocation source.

sites.notes: Count SMIC's Zhangjiang block once. The Pudong planning record places the SN1/SN2 plant project, filed by SMIC Shanghai, on the four-road block mapped as OSM way 300654142, and SMIC lists its Shanghai 200 mm and 300 mm fabs at 18 Zhangjiang Road on the same block (placement of No. 18 inferred from OpenStreetMap address geometry). Attribute advanced-node capability to SN1/SN2 only. The Ascend 910B relation rests on expert testimony and is not a first-party or universal allocation; TSMC also made 910B dies. The corrected OSM point is a representative point for a named industrial area, not a planning-area center or surveyed boundary.

all_product_relationships.caveat: EE Times (February 2025) reports that the Altera Agilex-7M FPGAs in Positron's Atlas are fabbed by Intel in Chandler, Arizona, and Business Insider (January 2025) says Positron's chips are made in Chandler; EE Times (February 2026) says Atlas still uses Agilex-7M. Intel calls Fab 52 its fifth high-volume fab at the Ocotillo campus in Chandler, and the Atlas records no other Intel wafer-fab campus there, so the campus link is an inference from city-level reports. Intel and Altera do not name the fab, no node, share, or volume is given, and the chip is Altera's general-purpose FPGA, not a Positron-designed die.

exact_campus_allocation.notes: Reports that Positron's Atlas is based on Altera Agilex-7M FPGAs with 32 GB HBM, fabricated by Intel (IFS) in Chandler, Arizona, and that a separate Positron ASIC was then only planned. Supports the corrected foundry fields for Positron Archer and the independently reported Archer relationship at Intel's Arizona / Ocotillo campus: Intel's high-volume Chandler fabs are on that campus. It names only the city, not a fab or process node, and says Positron aimed to make a later ASIC on TSMC N5 in Arizona.
exact_campus_allocation.title: Startup Positron Takes On Nvidia With FPGAs

exact_campus_allocation.notes: Business Insider (Emma Cosgrove) reports that "Positron's chips are made in Chandler, Arizona, by Intel-owned firm, Altera." Altera supplies the FPGAs and does not run wafer fabs; EE Times (AISRC-0247) says the Agilex-7M FPGAs are fabbed at Intel Foundry in Chandler. The article names only the city, not a fab, module, or process node. Cited through the Yahoo Finance syndicated copy.

product.notes: Positron's Atlas page lists eight Archer accelerators with 32 GB HBM each and says the system is shipping. EE Times reports that the first-generation Atlas uses Altera Agilex-7M FPGAs, not a TSMC ASIC, fabbed by Intel in Chandler, Arizona, and Business Insider likewise says Positron's chips are made in Chandler; Intel's high-volume Chandler fabs are on its Ocotillo campus, so the campus link is inferred from city-level reports. exact_campus_allocations.caveat: EE Times (February 2025) reports that the Altera Agilex-7M FPGAs in Positron's Atlas are fabbed by Intel in Chandler, Arizona, and Business Insider (January 2025) says Positron's chips are made in Chandler; EE Times (February 2026) says Atlas still uses Agilex-7M. site_capability.notes: Claim: TSMC reports that Kumamoto Fab 1 began volume production at end-2024, that the second fab is under construction and planned for 3 nm to meet AI-driven demand, and that 1.4 nm fab construction commenced in Taichung in 2025. Limitation: AI-driven demand is not a named-product allocation; the report does not resolve the A14 parcel boundary relative to Fab 15. Staging assessment: high_for_stated_claims. The report gives its printed date only in section 4.6.1 ('As of 03/01/2026 (Note)'; 'Note: The printed date of this Annual Report.'), so it is cited as March 1, 2026; April 16, 2026 is the filing date of TSMC's separate 2025 Form 20-F.
site_capability.title: TSMC 2025 Annual Report

site_capability.notes: TSMC's operating-fab table (fabs in operation as of February 28, 2026) identifies Fab 12, Fab 14, Fab 15, Fab 16, Fab 18, Fab 20, Fab 22, and Fab 23; gives commercial-production timing; reports the most advanced volume-production technology for each listed site as of year-end 2025; and describes continuing Fab 20 and Fab 22 expansion in 2026. Fab 23 is located in Kumamoto, Japan (commercial production 2024; 28 nm at year-end 2025); the filing states that JASM's manufacturing entity is Fab 23, that JASM volume production commenced in December 2024, and that construction on the second site commenced in October 2025. source_registry.notes: Quotes an April 2026 X post in which Tesla CEO Elon Musk wrote that AI6 would "deliver a true doubling of performance over AI5 in the same half reticle size using the Samsung 2nm fab in Texas" and that "AI6.5 will further improve performance using TSMC 2nm in Arizona." The article notes that Samsung is building its foundry in Taylor, Texas, and that Musk earlier indicated AI5, to be made by Samsung and TSMC, would enter mass production by mid-2027.
source_registry.title: Musk confirms Samsung, TSMC to produce future AI6 chips

source_registry.notes: Quotes a LinkedIn post in which Samsung Foundry principal engineer James Kim wrote that the Tesla-Samsung AI5 chip had reached tape-out and "is scheduled to be manufactured at the Taylor fab using our latest 2nm process." Reports that the TSMC version of AI5 taped out several months earlier and that AI5 is projected for Tesla's cars, robots, and data centers. The headline's "production starts soon" is the publisher's inference; the post reports a tape-out and a manufacturing plan, not Taylor output.
source_registry.title: Tesla's AI5 with 2nm-class node tapes out at Samsung Foundry — production starts soon, months after TSMC tape out

source_registry.notes: Reports the Samsung Foundry engineer's LinkedIn post on the AI5 tape-out and its planned manufacture at Taylor on 2 nm, and that he deleted the post after Korean outlets reported it. Says Samsung has said it expects volume production of Tesla's AI chips at Taylor in the second half of 2027, that Musk has said AI5 volume is not expected until mid-2027, and recalls Electrek's earlier report that AI6 mass production had slipped to "Q4 2027 at the earliest." The headline overstates: the post describes a tape-out and a manufacturing plan, not production.
source_registry.title: Samsung's Texas fab enters production for Tesla's AI5 chip on 2nm

source_registry.notes: Quotes Musk's X post of January 18, 2026: "AI5 will make the cars almost perfect and greatly enhance Optimus. AI6 will be for Optimus and data centers." Reports AI5 as aimed for early 2027.
source_registry.title: Musk Targets 9-Month Chip Cycle for Tesla; Talks AI5, AI6 and Space-Based AI

source_registry.notes: Reports Musk's April 15, 2026 X posts that AI5 had taped out and that its initial focus is "Optimus and our supercomputer clusters. AI4 is enough to achieve much better than human safety for FSD." Expects vehicle use no earlier than 2027 and reports AI6 as "slated for a 2028 production start," with Samsung manufacturing in the U.S.
source_registry.title: Musk Says Tesla's AI5 Chip is Done, Not Coming to Cars First

source_registry.notes: Quotes Musk's X post of November 4, 2025 that slightly different versions of AI5 will be made at TSMC and Samsung and that AI6 will "use the same fabs, but achieve roughly 2X performance." Reports Musk saying AI5 had not yet taped out and was scheduled to enter production in 2026, with AI6 about a year later.
source_registry.title: Musk confirms Tesla AI5 and AI6 will be made at both Samsung and TSMC, reinforcing dual-foundry strategy

source_registry.notes: Relays an anonymous Weibo post claiming that the TSMC-made portion of Tesla's AI6 family would move to Intel, and recalls Musk's April 2026 statement that AI6.5 would be made by TSMC in Arizona. Single-source and unconfirmed; the article itself calls the move unlikely.
source_registry.title: Tesla Reportedly Moving The Production Of Its AI6.5 Chip From TSMC To Intel "Under The Pressure And Insistence Of The Trump Administration"

source_registry.notes: Business Insider (Emma Cosgrove) reports that "Positron's chips are made in Chandler, Arizona, by Intel-owned firm, Altera."
